title: Selective eval harness for customer model pins and catalog upgrades
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Automatically run a small, targeted evaluation (a 'litmus' harness) when a model version is pinned or upgraded, whether the change originates in the public catalog or from a customer-pinned override. The harness should be selective (not full-scale evals) and produce concise delta reports to inform rollouts, surface regressions early, and optionally block unsafe upgrades.

Motivation:
- Customers pin model versions to avoid surprise regressions; we need a lightweight guard that gives quick signal on quality delta before traffic shifts.
- Full eval suites are expensive; we should run focused tests drawn from the customer's representative prompt set plus a common cross-customer litmus set.
- Early automatic feedback reduces incident discovery windows and supports safer canary/cohort rollouts.

Acceptance criteria:
1) On model pin/upgrade events (catalog or customer), the system triggers a selective eval job scoped to: (a) customer-specific prompt set (if present), (b) shared litmus prompts for the model family.
2) Eval completes within an SLO (target: 10–30 minutes depending on payload), emits a delta report (metrics: exact-match, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, embedding-similarity, hallucination score, safety flags), and stores results in the eval-results bucket.
3) If any metric crosses configured thresholds (per-customer or global), the event is flagged and an alert is created in the Console with links to results and suggested actions (approve, roll back, run full eval).
4) Customers can opt-out or require manual approval in account settings. Admins can configure strict/lenient thresholds per workspace.
5) UI: Console shows a compact status card for pinned versions with last-litmus timestamp, delta summary, and quick actions.
6) Cost controls: limit concurrent litmus jobs, cap per-customer monthly litmus runs, and provide sampling (run on X% of pin events).

Scope & non-goals:
- Scope: design and implementation of the litmus orchestration, delta reporting format, Console surface for results, basic opt-in/opt-out controls, and integration with existing eval storage/dashboarding.
- Non-goal: running full large-scale eval suites or replacing the eval playbook for major releases (those remain separate and expensive).

Design options considered:
- Option A (preferred): Run a two-tier harness: 1) customer prompt set (if exists) limited to N prompts, 2) shared litmus of ~50 cross-cutting prompts. Use fast, approximate metrics (embedding sim + safety heuristics) to keep latency low.
- Option B: Run only shared litmus by default, require explicit customer prompt set to be uploaded to trigger per-customer check. Less coverage but lower cost.

Trade-offs:
- Speed vs. coverage: More prompts increase statistical confidence but cost and duration. We bias for fast signals that catch high-severity regressions (safety, hallucination) and regressions in high-traffic intents.
- Blocking semantics: Automatic block-on-fail reduces risk but increases friction for ops. We default to non-blocking with strong notifications and an optional workspace policy to enforce blocking.

Implementation notes / integration points:
- Trigger points: catalog upgrade pipeline (model catalog service), and customer pin API (pins service). Both should emit a standard event to 'pin-eval-orchestrator'.
- Orchestrator will enqueue a litmus job in the eval queue with priority tags (catalog vs customer). Job runner uses the same eval infra but with a lightweight suite profile.
- Results stored to: s3://redwood-eval-results/pin-litmus/{workspace}/{model}/{revision}/{run_ts}. JSON delta report schema v1.
- Notifications: Console notification + workspace email + webhook. Include links to the run and a one-click run-full-eval action.
- Observability: instrument latency, failure rate, cost per-eval, false-positive rate (via manual overrides), and time-to-action after alert.

Open implementation decisions (to resolve with Eng):
- Exact size of the shared litmus set (propose 50 prompts to start).
- Default enforcement policy for catalog-originated upgrades vs customer pins (catalog upgrades: non-blocking, notify infra/owners; customer workspace policy may allow blocking).
- Per-customer storage of representative prompts: format, privacy guarantees, and retention policy.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QG/Pin+Litmus+Design
- Initial design sketch (Figma): https://figma.com/file/abcd1234/pin-litmus
- Backend spike PR (prototype runner): https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/1234
- Example delta report schema: https://gist.github.com/redwood-inference/pin-litmus-schema

Security & compliance:
- Customer prompt sets are treated as sensitive workspace data. Storage follows workspace encryption keys and RBAC; do not surface prompt contents in public dashboards.
- security_review_required: false for minimal harness, but escalate if we add personnel-sensitive prompt sharing.

Rollout plan:
1) Stage feature behind a feature flag for internal workspaces.
2) Run internal-only litmus on all internal catalog upgrades for 2 weeks, tune thresholds.
3) Opt-in beta for 5 customer workspaces; gather feedback and false-positive metrics.
4) Gradual wide rollout with sampling and quotas.

Success metrics:
- Litmus run latency median < 20 minutes.
- True-positive regression detection for top-5 incidents that would have otherwise led to customer-visible regressions.
- Reduction in post-deploy regression incidents by 30% in first quarter after rollout.

Notes on follow-ups:
- Integrate with rollout automation to allow automated canary size reduction on litmus fail.
- Add a 're-run with pinned seeds' flow for debugging failures.
